title: First accepting payload within a step bound
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with state set $S$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ assign a configuration of $M$ on $x$ to each natural number. Let $a$ assign a Boolean acceptance flag and $y$ a Boolean payload word to each natural number, and let $B,N$ be natural numbers. Suppose $c(N)$ is halted with empty output. Suppose also that for every $j<N$ there is a time $t\le B$ such that, if $a(j)$ is true, the run from $c(j)$ is halted at time $t$ with output $y(j)$; if $a(j)$ is false, the run from $c(j)$ at time $t$ is exactly $c(j+1)$. Then from $c(0)$ the machine halts within $N B$ steps with output $y(i)$ for the first index $i<N$ with $a(i)$ true, if such an index exists, and with empty output if none exists.
hypotheses_covered: multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with state set S
configuration sequence c on input x
c(N) is halted with empty output
for every j<N, some t≤B satisfies the acceptance-dependent run condition
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c_0, \dots, c_N$
be configurations of $M$ on a common input with $c_N$ halted with empty output, let $a$
be a Boolean predicate on round indices, and let $w$ assign a payload word to each
index. Assume for each $j < N$ that within $B$ steps the machine either halts from $c_j$
with output $w(j)$ (when $a(j)$ holds) or reaches $c_{j+1}$ (when $a(j)$ fails). Then
from $c_0$ the machine halts within $N \cdot B$ steps, with output $w(i)$ for the least
accepting index $i < N$ when one exists and empty output otherwise.
